title: Amazon may get Decart for $5.5 billion after Anthropic walked away
source_used: CTech (Calcalist), read from the article body in the page data
key_facts: CTech (Calcalist) reports a proposed Amazon purchase of Decart valuing the company at $5.5 billion, below the $7 billion reported by the Wall Street Journal and less than Anthropic was reportedly prepared to pay.
A deal could be signed by the end of October, per Calcalist.
About a month ago Anthropic decided not to acquire Decart, reportedly after due diligence; Decart said it was unwilling to relocate to the US, an explanation Calcalist says few found convincing.
After that, Decart tried to reopen talks with Nvidia, which had made the first serious offer, and Nvidia declined; shareholders then turned to Amazon.
Decart's last funding round, in May 2026, valued it at $4 billion (total funding more than $450 million); it has fewer than 100 employees and revenue of tens of millions of dollars.

Decart has worked with Amazon almost since its start; its software helps AI models run efficiently on chips from different makers, and Amazon is developing its own Trainium chips to reduce reliance on Nvidia.
Decart did not comment on the reports.
quote_evidence: Calcalist has learned that after the Anthropic deal fell through, Decart tried to reopen negotiations with Nvidia, which had made the first serious acquisition offer before Anthropic entered the picture.

According to information obtained by Calcalist, the proposed transaction would value Decart at $5.5 billion, below the $7 billion figure reported by The Wall Street Journal and less than Anthropic was reportedly prepared to pay.
Decart did not comment on reports of a potential sale to Amazon.
why_it_matters_hint: Amazon's reported price is lower than earlier reports, and Decart's software could help Amazon's own chips compete with Nvidia's.
